label: Pooled batched attention
mechanism: decode attention core batched over per-layer KV batch pools — one ~20-op chain per layer instead of per row
hypothesis: Ranked-next (2) from the exp-0005 profile row: attn_core is 1646 ms of the 1989 ms B=64 step and the step is host-enqueue-bound (132,221 launches/step, GPU busy 31-33%) because attn_decode_batch runs a per-ROW Python core — 64 rows x 66 layers x ~20 eager ops plus the kv.PagedKV._flat_slots .tolist() sync 2 x 11 x B times per step. This diff gives each layer a batch pool (kv.SwaPool: the 64 rings as rows of one tensor; kv.GlobalPool: one shared page pool + device-side page-table mirror) with per-seq RingKV/PagedKV becoming views/handles into pool slots, so prefill runs the exact per-seq code (bitwise; TF gate numbers unchanged from main: 0.955/0.05065/0.600919) while the decode core collapses to per-layer batched ops: one index_put_ append, one padded gather, batched rel-bias/tau, one broadcast GQA matmul, masked-selection softmax, @V — no .tolist() anywhere in the step. Measured in-process on this exact build (one load, same 64 prefilled canonical-distribution seqs, ISL~736, /workspace/logs/t_pooled_exp0007_2026-07-30.log): old core 2010.9 ms/step (31.8 tok/s; reproduces exp-0005's 1989 ms), pooled core 485.4 ms/step (131.9 tok/s) — 4.14x step wall.
predicted_delta: +75-115% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s (21.5 -> ~38-46; the bench model tok_s = 128/((128/64)*step_s + 1.93 s serialized prefill) reproduces exp-0006's measured 21.5 at step 2.01 s and gives 44.1 at step 0.485 s; prefill admission serialization then becomes the binding constraint — chunked/batched prefill is the ranked next attack, per-step profile attribution second)

local_pregate.determinism: batch row order stays admission order (unchanged); slot ids only select pool rows, never order; every index tensor (ring slots, page tables, validity masks) is a pure function of the schedule; stale pool slots are excluded by masked_fill SELECTION (garbage-proof: overwrite, never add), matching how the per-seq gather simply omitted them. t_batched arm C bitwise PASS is the same-schedule gate the worker's determinism arm re-runs at bench scale.
local_pregate.memory: pools pre-allocate exactly max_batch per-seq KV footprints (SwaPool = 64 rings/layer, GlobalPool = 64 x 1024 pages/layer) — identical total to exp-0006 at full occupancy, verified live: server ready on 4 GPUs with pools + weights, TF gate green; exp-0005's B=64 arms already ran this occupancy.
